entries.clue: Study dark period in Germany’s western province (8)

blocks.note: to con a text is to study it closely
Nacht is German for night

annotation.surface: A spell of darkness somewhere in the west of Germany.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Germany’s western province' reads as one phrase and is two jobs: Germany supplies the language, and the province lies elsewhere entirely. The apostrophe-s is standing in for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Connacht is the westernmost of Ireland's four historic provinces, the land beyond the Shannon.

entries.clue: Note disease’s culmination in pink colour of part of the eye (7)

indicatorNotes.culmination: A culmination is the point a thing finally reaches, so only the last letter of the word before it is wanted.
indicatorNotes.in: What is in something sits inside it, so the two letters named are planted within the colour.

blocks.note: coral is a pink, named after the reef animal's skeleton
n = note
the last letter of DISEASE

annotation.surface: A written note on how an illness ended, set down in pink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' is N from the dictionary abbreviation, not from the musical scale, which is where a solver looks first. The definition is adjectival: it describes something belonging to the eye's clear front layer rather than naming the layer.
annotation.definitionFit: The answer is the adjective formed from the clear dome at the front of the eye, so it means belonging to that part of it.

entries.clue: Assassin popular in New Jersey area (5)

indicatorNotes.in: Whatever is in a place sits within it, so the two letters named are taken inside the state's initials, splitting them apart.

blocks.note: NJ is the postal abbreviation for New Jersey
whatever is in at the moment is popular
a = area

annotation.surface: A hired killer who is well liked in one part of New Jersey.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Popular' is the crossword's standard way of asking for IN, which leaves the little word 'in' itself free to be the instruction. New Jersey gives up its postal pair and is prised open.
annotation.definitionFit: Ninjas were the covert agents of feudal Japan, trained for stealth killings, so the answer is one kind of assassin.

entries.clue: An article put out by perturbed mathematician re: statistical concept (10,4)

indicatorNotes.put out by: To be put out by something is to be evicted from it, so the letter named leaves the letters that follow.
indicatorNotes.perturbed: Anything perturbed has been thrown out of its settled state, so the letters may be taken in any order at all.

blocks.note: A is the indefinite article, and it is the single letter taken away
MATHEMATICIAN RE with that A gone, 14 letters

annotation.surface: A paper withdrawn by an agitated mathematician.
annotation.walkthrough: 'An article' is the letter A itself rather than a piece of writing, which is why the fodder comes up a letter short of the words it is drawn from. The colon after 're' dresses it up as a subject heading.
annotation.definitionFit: The arithmetic mean is the ordinary average — add the values and divide by how many there are — and statistics is where it is given that name.

entries.clue: Is upset, putting on gardener’s unknown stockings? (7)

annotation.definitionNote: Hosiery is a collective singular where 'stockings' is a plural, but the two name the same goods on the same shop shelf.

indicatorNotes.upset: Something upset has been turned over, and in a down clue that means its letters now read upward.
indicatorNotes.putting on: You put on a garment by climbing inside it, so whatever does the putting on ends up wrapped by what follows.

blocks.note: someone working a hoe is a hoer
the word IS, read the other way up
y = unknown, algebra's stand-in for a value not yet found

annotation.surface: Someone toppling over while pulling on the gardener's peculiar stockings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unknown' reads as mysterious and is algebra's y. 'Putting on' is the picture and the instruction at the same time, because what you put on goes round you.
annotation.definitionFit: Hosiery is the trade's word for stockings, tights and socks — knitted legwear sold as a class.

entries.clue: Uncomfortable feeling one gets around hospital (4)

indicatorNotes.gets around: To get around something is to pass all the way round it, so the letters named close over the next piece.

blocks.note: the ace is the one of a suit
h = hospital

annotation.surface: The queasiness a person feels in the neighbourhood of a hospital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One' as ACE comes from cards, where the ace counts as one. The clue also runs straight through as a plain remark about how hospitals make visitors feel.
annotation.definitionFit: An ache is the dull, lasting sort of pain rather than a sharp one — discomfort you carry about with you.

entries.clue: Nice socks, fancy, producing overconfidence (9)

indicatorNotes.fancy: Fancy work is decorated and reworked rather than left plain, so the letters named have been done over into a new arrangement.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A compliment paid to someone about their smart socks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nice socks' looks like praise being offered, so 'fancy' reads as more of the same; it is the instruction. The commas fence it off from both the socks and the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Cockiness is self-assurance carried too far, the strutting sort that has stopped allowing for being wrong.

entries.clue: Quotation from withdrawn religious publication? (7)

blocks.note: ex = out of, the prefix for something taken away from where it was
a tract is a short religious pamphlet handed out to passers-by

annotation.surface: A line quoted from a religious pamphlet taken out of circulation.
annotation.walkthrough: A tract is the small religious pamphlet pressed on you in the street. 'Withdrawn' hands over EX, the prefix meaning out of, rather than describing a shy person.
annotation.definitionFit: An extract is a passage lifted out of a longer text and reproduced on its own, which is what a quotation is.

entries.clue: A special triple variable solar phenomenon (7,7)

indicatorNotes.variable: What is variable holds no fixed form, so the letters named are free to settle in any arrangement.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

annotation.surface: A three-part special offer whose terms keep changing.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder is the clue's whole first half, the opening 'A' included, which is the letter most often left behind when a clue starts with it. 'Variable' sits where an adjective would and carries the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A partial eclipse is what you see when the moon covers only some of the sun's disc, leaving a bright crescent behind.

entries.clue: Ancient character I attached to British monarchy (6)

blocks.note: b = British
a rune is a letter of the old Germanic alphabets
the letter I, taken exactly as it stands

annotation.surface: An ancient figure who claims to be attached to the British crown.
annotation.walkthrough: A rune is a letter of the old Germanic alphabets, cut into stone or wood. 'Ancient character' first reads as a person from long ago, and 'British monarchy' as a single phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small oil-rich sultanate on Borneo whose sultan rules absolutely, so it is a monarchy outright.

entries.clue: Musical recalled one of its contributors with old way of playing (8)

indicatorNotes.recalled: To recall something is to call it back, and letters called back arrive in the reverse of the order they left in.

blocks.note: CATS is the musical, turned back to front
the cast of that musical is cats, so one of them is a CAT
o = old

annotation.surface: A show brought to mind along with one of the performers who made it.
annotation.walkthrough: Cats is the Lloyd Webber musical whose entire cast plays cats, which is what lets 'one of its contributors' be a single animal rather than a writer or a backer.
annotation.definitionFit: Staccato marks notes to be played short and detached, each clipped off before the next, so it describes a manner of playing.

entries.clue: Troops behaving impartially (10)

annotation.definitionNote: The second half names the conduct where the answer names the quality behind it, letting a description of what someone does stand for the noun.

blocks.note: the military reading: a party of soldiers detached for a particular duty
the second reading: the cool even-handedness of someone with no stake in the matter

annotation.surface: Soldiers keeping themselves out of a quarrel.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses come from the same verb, detach: a unit sent off on its own errand, and a mind held at a distance from what it is judging. Four words with no instruction in them at all.
annotation.definitionFit: A detachment is a party of soldiers split off for a particular duty; detachment is also the aloof even-handedness of someone with nothing at stake.

entries.clue: Native of Arab state expressing cheers, backing Arab state (4)

indicatorNotes.expressing: To express something is to press it out, the way juice is got from a lemon, so the letters named are squeezed from the word holding them.
indicatorNotes.backing: Backing is going backwards, so what is left is read from its last letter round to its first.

blocks.note: a Qatari is a native of Qatar
'ta' is the everyday British thank-you, and pressing it out of QATARI leaves QARI

annotation.surface: Someone from one Gulf country raising a glass in support of another.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Expressing' is where the clue turns: not saying a thing but squeezing it out. The two Arab states named are different countries, one in the wordplay and one in the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Iraq is an Arabic-speaking republic between Syria and Iran and a founding member of the Arab League.

entries.clue: Confused body of men heading off into race (8)

indicatorNotes.heading off: A word's head is its first letter, and heading it off takes that letter clean away.
indicatorNotes.into: Going into something means ending up inside it, so what is left lands within the other word.

blocks.note: to fly along is to race
a MUSTER is an assembled body of men, with its head letter gone

annotation.surface: A muddled group of men setting off into a race.
annotation.walkthrough: A muster is a body of men assembled on parade. 'Heading off' reads as setting out, which is the sense the surface needs before you take a first letter away.
annotation.definitionFit: Flustery describes someone in a flap, agitated and unable to keep their thoughts in order.

entries.clue: Colleague in a rush getting organised? Truly a professional (9)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition describes the man rather than naming him, and the question mark earlier in the clue carries that stretch.

indicatorNotes.in: What is in something sits inside it, so the colleague's four letters land within the reordered ones.
indicatorNotes.getting organised: Getting organised means being put into a different arrangement, which is what happens to the letters named.

blocks.note: A RUSH reordered, then split to take the next chunk
a mate is a colleague

annotation.surface: A workmate hurrying to get himself sorted out, and making a real job of it.
annotation.walkthrough: The word belongs to the old row in rugby union and athletics over sportsmen who kept their amateur status while quietly being paid. 'In' is both the surface's preposition and the instruction to insert.
annotation.definitionFit: The answer names a supposed amateur who is paid like a professional, so 'truly a professional' is what he is underneath the label.

entries.clue: Stops state troubles with withdrawal of currency (6)

indicatorNotes.withdrawal of: A withdrawal takes something out of where it was lodged, so the money named is drawn out of the word holding it.

blocks.note: to aver something is to state it firmly
TROUBLES with ROUBLE taken out of it leaves T and S
the rouble is Russia's currency, and these are the letters withdrawn

annotation.surface: A government heading off unrest by taking money out of circulation.
annotation.walkthrough: The rouble sits whole and unbroken inside TROUBLES, which is the sort of hiding a solver finds only by reading the word letter by letter. 'State' is the verb here, not a country.
annotation.definitionFit: To avert something is to turn it aside before it arrives, so it stops the thing from ever happening.

entries.clue: Henry II touring most of far state (6)

indicatorNotes.touring: A tour goes right round its destination, so the king's two chunks travel around what sits between them.
indicatorNotes.most of: Most of a word is all but a little of it, so its final letter is left behind.

blocks.note: h = henry, the unit of inductance
far is AWAY, cut short of its last letter
II is two in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: King Henry II riding round a distant corner of his realm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Henry II' is one English king on the surface and two crossword pieces underneath, the unit of inductance and the Roman two. The pair parts company to let the middle chunk sit between them.
annotation.definitionFit: Hawaii is the fiftieth state of the USA, a chain of Pacific islands two thousand miles off the mainland.

entries.clue: Car hire firm investing in provider of cash showing very traditional attitude (7)

indicatorNotes.investing in: Money invested goes into the thing it is put towards, so the firm named ends up inside what follows.

blocks.note: an ATM is the cash machine in the wall
Avis is one of the big international car rental chains

annotation.surface: A car rental chain buying its way into the cash-machine business.
annotation.walkthrough: The word is the biologist's term for an ancestral trait resurfacing generations later, which is how an outlook comes to be called a throwback. 'Investing in' does double duty, the money of the surface and the insertion of the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: The answer names a reversion to an ancestral form, so an outlook that reverts to how things were done long ago counts as one.

entries.clue: Expression of gratitude not so much found in Times - almost forbidden (5,3)

indicatorNotes.found in: Whatever is found in a thing was sitting inside it, so the chunk named goes between the other's two letters.
indicatorNotes.almost: Almost there is not quite there, so the word stops one letter short of its end.

blocks.note: three times four is three by four, so 'times' is BY
less of a thing is not so much of it
something forbidden is OUT, docked of its last letter

annotation.surface: Thanks turning up less and less in the Times, and all but banned there.
annotation.walkthrough: The italics push the newspaper at you, and the word is the multiplication sign, which in speech is 'by'. Saying something is out is how a rule gets announced without the word forbidden.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Bless you' is said in thanks for a kindness as readily as after a sneeze, a warm way of putting thank you.

entries.clue: Qualified teacher put out, being called up when they want to sleep? (7)

indicatorNotes.being called up: Calling something up brings it upward, and in a down clue letters that come up read backwards.

blocks.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education, the British teaching degree
to put out is to EMIT, here turned round

annotation.surface: A trained teacher annoyed at being telephoned just as they are ready for sleep.
annotation.walkthrough: BEd is the British teaching degree, a Bachelor of Education. 'Put out' is the trap: it reads as offended, and has to mean emit before there is anything to turn round.
annotation.definitionFit: Bedtime is the hour at which someone is due to turn in, which is exactly when they want to sleep.

entries.clue: Marsupial work needing very large amount (7)

blocks.note: op = opus, a composer's numbered work
OS is outsize, the British clothing label for very large
a sum is an amount of money

annotation.surface: A job that will need a very large sum of money.
annotation.walkthrough: OS is the outsize label sewn into British clothing, and OP the abbreviation stamped on a composer's numbered works. The definition is the single word at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: The opossum is the only marsupial native to North America, carrying its young in a pouch like its Australian relatives.

entries.clue: Luther’s agreement to bring in version of Bible for Asian island (4)

indicatorNotes.to bring in: To bring something in is to take it inside, so the letters named open up and close round what follows.

blocks.note: Luther was German, and ja is German for yes
AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible of 1611

annotation.surface: Martin Luther agreeing to take in a particular version of the Bible.
annotation.walkthrough: Luther is the German reformer, so his yes comes out in German. AV is the Authorised Version, one of the two Bible abbreviations a solver wants ready, the other being RV for the Revised.
annotation.definitionFit: Java is the Indonesian island that holds Jakarta, the most populous island on earth and squarely in Asia.

entries.clue: Reasonably intellectual Bishop occupying spot halfway down the stalls? (10)

indicatorNotes.occupying: To occupy a seat is to sit right in it, so the piece named settles inside the words that follow.

blocks.note: a seat halfway back in the stalls is in the middle row
b = bishop, the chess piece

annotation.surface: A bishop sitting halfway back in the stalls at the theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: The stalls are the ground-floor seats of a British theatre, so 'halfway down the stalls' offers a place to sit rather than a place in a word. B is the chess bishop.
annotation.definitionFit: Middlebrow work aims between the popular and the demanding, so its audience is taken to be reasonably rather than seriously intellectual.

entries.clue: Pub bringing in beer finally with one pipe (5)

indicatorNotes.bringing in: Bringing something in takes it inside, so the letters named open up to hold what comes next.
indicatorNotes.finally: Finally points at the end, so only the last letter of the word before it is wanted.

blocks.note: the bar is the pub
the last letter of BEER
i = one, the Roman numeral

annotation.surface: A pub taking in the last of the beer along with a single pipe.
annotation.walkthrough: The pipe here is turned from the hard root-burl of the tree heath that grows round the Mediterranean, and smokers name the pipe after that wood. 'Finally' is the standard call for a last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Pipes of this kind are cut from heath root, and the wood's name has become the everyday word for the pipe itself.

entries.clue: Quantity of American wine at one gathering of readers? (8)

annotation.definitionNote: The literati are a class of people rather than an assembly of them, and the question mark owns that looseness.

blocks.note: a litre of wine, spelt the American way
the word at, taken exactly as it stands
i = one, the Roman numeral

annotation.surface: A litre of wine at a party for bookish people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of American' is doing spelling work rather than naming a country: it asks for the US form of the metric measure. The two words that follow it are simply set down as they stand.
annotation.definitionFit: The literati are the well-read taken as a body — the writers, critics and scholars of a country.

entries.clue: Unduly fussy to snoop around orbiting vehicle (6)

indicatorNotes.around: What goes around a thing encloses it, so the letters named wrap the next chunk.

blocks.note: to pry is to snoop
the ISS is the International Space Station, circling the earth since 1998

annotation.surface: A busybody nosing about a craft in orbit.
annotation.walkthrough: The ISS is the International Space Station, the crewed laboratory that has circled the earth since 1998. 'Orbiting' describes it on the surface, while 'around' is what does the enclosing.
annotation.definitionFit: Prissy describes someone primly and excessively concerned with neatness and propriety, fussy past what the occasion asks for.

entries.clue: Muddy border turned over before end of day (4)

indicatorNotes.turned over: Turning something over reverses it, so its letters run from the last one back to the first.
indicatorNotes.end of: The end of a word is its final letter, and that letter alone is wanted.

blocks.note: a RIM is a border, read backwards
the last letter of DAY

annotation.surface: A flowerbed edging flipped over as the day closes.
annotation.walkthrough: A rim is a border, and 'turned over' asks for it backwards. 'End of day' offers dusk first and delivers a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Miry means boggy and plastered with mud, the state of ground churned into mire.

entries.clue: Message from overseas: ROUTE’S LAST STAGE ABOARD PUBLIC TRANSPORT (8)

indicatorNotes.LAST: Last points at the end of a word, so only its final letter is taken.
indicatorNotes.ABOARD: To go aboard is to climb inside the vehicle, so the letters named sit within it.

blocks.note: a tram is public transport, and it opens up to take the rest
the last letter of ROUTE
a leg of a journey is a stage of it

annotation.surface: The closing stretch of a route, covered on public transport.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals are the joke: these were printed in upper case and delivered on a strip of paper. A leg is a stage of a journey, and 'aboard' is the word a tram naturally attracts.
annotation.definitionFit: Before the telephone a message crossing an ocean came by cable and was delivered on paper as a telegram.
